Jordan / Ben —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the checklist and drafted a very narrow redline for the MSA/Order Form to minimize Procurement friction. High level: we recommend the limited "Option 2" approach that requires prior written approval for press mentions but permits logo use for case studies or marketing materials with an explicit opt-in checkbox on the Order Form. This keeps us flexible while respecting Novatech's control.

Key proposed edits (high-level):
- Replace broad "non-exclusive, revocable right" language with: "Customer may opt-in to allow Redwood to use Customer's name and logo for marketing purposes. Any press release referencing the Customer requires prior written approval. Logo use for case studies or Redwood marketing shall be limited to the assets listed in the attached checklist and subject to Customer's brand guidelines."
- Add a 30-day approval window for press drafts after Redwood submits a draft for review. If Customer does not respond within 30 days, approval is deemed withheld (we will not publish).
- Add a short evidence trail clause: requests for approval should reference the order number and be archived by both parties for 12 months. (This is a light retention ask to aid procurement audits.)

I attach: 
- Redwood_MSA_publicity_redline_20260427.docx (track changes)
- A one-page summary we can send to Novatech explaining the minimal changes.

If Jordan is comfortable I suggest we send the redline and the one-page summary to Sara and CC procurement/legal at Novatech so they see this is lightweight.

—Marissa
